chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qoob narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from his father, from Shurahbeel, who said: Abu Ja'far (and I had asked him about al-Qa'im)
He said: He will not appear until a caller from the Heaven calls out, and the people of the East and the West will hear it, until the girl in her chamber hears it.

key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: The Riser (al-Qa'im), a title for the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What is the celestial sign that precedes the appearance of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) identifies the celestial announcement as a definitive prelude to the Mahdi's appearance, emphasizing its universal audibility to signify the end of the era of concealment. This event serves as a major eschatological sign, bridging the gap between the hidden Imam and the global community, ensuring no soul remains unaware of the dawn of justice.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (14) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ahmad bin Yousuf bin Ya’qoob from Issma’eel bin Mihran from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abu Hamza from his father from Shurahbeel that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said when he had been asked about al-Qa’im:
“Al-Qa’im does not appear until a caller from the Heaven will call out that everyone in the east and in the west will hear the call even the girls in their veils.”
